name: Field Doctor-Style Beef Bolognese + Penne (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
670 g Penne Pasta (GLUTEN FREE) [brown rice flour]
1 1/2 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
370 g Extra Lean Beef
3 medium Carrots
1 1/4 Red Peppers
160 g Spinach
85 g Tomato Puree [tomato]
65 g Parmigiano (MILK) [MILK Salt, Microbial Enzymes]
45 g Fennel
30 g Kalamata Olives [olives, water, salt, red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil]
9 tbsp Mixed Herbs
6 tbsp Parsley Flat
22 g Sundried Tomatoes [Sundried tomatoes, Salt]
2 1/2 tbsp Tapioca Starch
3/4 tbsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
3/4 tbsp Red Wine Vinegar
2 tsp Beef Stock [Beef Extract, Water, Salt]
1 3/4 tsp Sea Salt
1 1/4 tbsp Sweet Noble Paprika
6.6 g Chives
3/4 tbsp Black Pepper
directions:
1. Pasta: Cook gluten-free brown-rice penne until al dente; drain, keep a little cooking water.

2. Ragu: Brown extra-lean beef in extra virgin olive oil. Soften carrot, red pepper, fennel and chives. Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, sundried tomatoes, olives, beef stock, tamari, red wine vinegar, sweet paprika, herb mix and black pepper. Simmer 20–30 minutes until rich; thicken with tapioca slurry if needed.

3. Finish: Wilt spinach into the ragu. Toss with penne, loosening with pasta water. Serve with hard cheese and parsley.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Penne Pasta (GLUTEN FREE) [brown rice flour], Chopped Tomato, Extra Lean Beef, Water, Carrot, Red Pepper, Spinach, Extra Virgin Olive Oil...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Beef Bolognese + Penne (Low FODMAP) (~381 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/beef-ragu-penne
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~381 g x 8 = 3048 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~354 g (inferred ~11.60% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~119 g (3.9% on label) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
